title: Sign-in endpoints are rate-limited with honest Retry-After
asA: operator on a service that will get hit with mint floods and token-guessing sweeps
iWant: POST /login and GET /login/verify both to reject beyond a configured ceiling with a 429 and a Retry-After the client can trust
soThat: the endpoints stop misfiring on abuse traffic without any WAF in the path

acceptanceCriteria.description: POST /login rejects with 429 once its ceiling is crossed within the configured window; the response carries a Retry-After header whose value is a positive integer or an HTTP-date not earlier than the request time.
acceptanceCriteria.given: POST /login is called from one client key beyond its ceiling within the window
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response status is 429 and Retry-After is present with a positive integer or a valid HTTP-date at or after request time

acceptanceCriteria.description: GET /login/verify rejects with 429 once its ceiling is crossed within the configured window; the response carries a Retry-After header.
acceptanceCriteria.given: GET /login/verify is called from one client key beyond its ceiling within the window
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response status is 429 and Retry-After is present

acceptanceCriteria.description: A 429 response from either endpoint does not disclose registration state; the response body is generic and identical across principals.
acceptanceCriteria.given: POST /login is rate-limited under registered and unregistered submissions in turn

acceptanceCriteria.description: The blueprint's default ceiling for POST /login is five requests per minute per client key; the ceiling is a project-configurable option.
acceptanceCriteria.given: POST /login runs with no project override
acceptanceCriteria.then: the ceiling is five requests per minute per client key; when the project supplies rateLimit={ max, timeWindow } the effective ceiling matches the override
